{{Short description|Group of irregular uniform polytopes}}
[[File:E8Petrie.svg|thumb|The [[4 21 polytope|''4''<sub>''21''</sub>]] polytope of 8-space<br>{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}]]
In [[geometry]], the '''Gosset–Elte figures''', named by [[Coxeter]] after [[Thorold Gosset]] and [[E. L. Elte]], are a group of [[uniform polytope]]s which are not [[regular polytopes|regular]], generated by a [[Wythoff construction]] with mirrors all related by order-2 and order-3 dihedral angles. They can be seen as ''one-end-ringed'' [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Finite Coxeter groups|Coxeter–Dynkin diagrams]].

The '''Coxeter symbol''' for these figures has the form '''''k''<sub>''i,j''</sub>''', where each letter represents a length of order-3 branches on a Coxeter–Dynkin diagram with a single ring on the end node of a ''k''-length sequence of branches. The [[vertex figure]] of ''k''<sub>''i,j''</sub> is (''k''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)<sub>''i,j''</sub>, and each of its facets are represented by subtracting one from one of the nonzero subscripts, i.e. ''k''<sub>''i''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1'',j''</sub> and ''k''<sub>''i,j''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1</sub>.<ref>Coxeter 1973, p. 201</ref>

Rectified [[simplex|simplices]] are included in the list as limiting cases with ''k'' = 0. Similarly ''0''<sub>''i,j,k''</sub> represents a bifurcated graph with a central node ringed.

== History ==
[[Coxeter]] named these figures as ''k''<sub>''i,j''</sub> (or ''k''<sub>''ij''</sub>)  in shorthand and gave credit of their discovery to Gosset and Elte:<ref>Coxeter, 1973, p. 210 (11.x Historical remarks)</ref>
* [[Thorold Gosset]] first published a list of ''regular and semi-regular figures in space of ''n'' dimensions''<ref>Gosset, 1900</ref> in 1900, enumerating polytopes with one or more types of [[regular polytope]] faces. This included the [[rectified 5-cell]] ''0''<sub>''21''</sub> in 4-space, [[demipenteract]] ''1''<sub>''21''</sub> in 5-space, [[2 21 polytope|''2''<sub>''21''</sub>]] in 6-space, [[3 21 polytope|''3''<sub>''21''</sub>]] in 7-space, [[4 21 polytope|''4''<sub>''21''</sub>]] in 8-space, and [[5 21 honeycomb|''5''<sub>''21''</sub>]] infinite tessellation in 8-space.
* [[E. L. Elte]] independently enumerated a different semiregular list in his 1912 book, ''The Semiregular Polytopes of the Hyperspaces''.<ref>E.L. Elte, 1912 Groningen (2006 Michigan)</ref> He called them ''semiregular polytopes of the first kind'', limiting his search to one or two types of regular or semiregular ''k''-faces.

Elte's enumeration included all the ''k''<sub>''ij''</sub> polytopes except for the [[1 42 polytope|''1''<sub>''42''</sub>]] which has 3 types of 6-faces.

The set of figures extend into honeycombs of (2,2,2), (3,3,1), and (5,4,1) families in 6,7,8 dimensional Euclidean spaces respectively. Gosset's list included the ''5''<sub>''21''</sub> honeycomb as the only semiregular one in his definition.

== Definition ==
[[File:Simply Laced Dynkin Diagrams.svg|thumb|Simply-laced ADE groups]]
The polytopes and honeycombs in this family can be seen within [[ADE classification]].

A finite polytope ''k''<sub>''ij''</sub> exists if
:<math>\frac{1}{i+1}+\frac{1}{j+1}+\frac{1}{k+1}>1</math>
or equal for Euclidean honeycombs, and less for hyperbolic honeycombs.

The [[Coxeter group]] '''[3<sup>i,j,k</sup>]''' can generate up to 3 unique uniform '''Gosset–Elte figures''' with [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram]]s with one end node ringed. By [[Coxeter]]'s notation, each figure is represented by '''''k<sub>ij</sub>''''' to mean the end-node on the ''k''-length sequence is ringed.

The [[simplex]] family can be seen as a limiting case with ''k'' = 0, and all [[Rectification (geometry)|rectified]] (single-ring) Coxeter–Dynkin diagrams.

== A-family [3<sup>''n''</sup>] (rectified simplices) ==
The family of ''n''-[[simplex|simplices]] contain Gosset–Elte figures of the form '''0<sub>''ij''</sub>''' as all [[Rectification (geometry)|rectified]] forms of the ''n''-simplex (''i''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''j''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1).

They are listed below, along with their [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram]], with each dimensional family drawn as a graphic [[orthogonal projection]] in the plane of the [[Petrie polygon]] of the regular simplex.

== D-family [3<sup>''n''&minus;3,1,1</sup>] demihypercube ==
Each D<sub>n</sub> group has two Gosset–Elte figures, the ''n''-[[demihypercube]] as '''1<sub>''k''1</sub>''', and an alternated form of the ''n''-[[orthoplex]], '''''k''<sub>11</sub>''', constructed with alternating simplex facets. Rectified ''n''-[[demihypercube]]s, a lower symmetry form of a birectified ''n''-cube, can also be represented as '''0<sub>''k''11</sub>'''.

==''E''<sub>''n''</sub> family [3<sup>''n''&minus;4,2,1</sup>] ==
Each E<sub>n</sub> group from 4 to 8 has two or three Gosset–Elte figures, represented by one of the end-nodes ringed: [[Semiregular k 21 polytope|'''''k''<sub>21</sub>''']], [[Uniform 1 k2 polytope|'''1<sub>''k''2</sub>''']], [[Uniform 2 k1 polytope|'''2<sub>''k''1</sub>''']]. A rectified '''1<sub>''k''2</sub>''' series can also be represented as '''0<sub>''k''21</sub>'''.

== Euclidean and hyperbolic honeycombs ==
There are three Euclidean ([[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Affine Coxeter groups|affine]]) [[Coxeter group]]s in dimensions 6, 7, and 8:<ref>Coxeter 1973, pp. 202–204, 11.8 Gosset's figures in six, seven, and eight dimensions.</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
!Coxeter group
!colspan=4|Honeycombs
|-
| <math>{\tilde{E}}_6</math> = [3<sup>2,2,2</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node|3|node_1}} = [[2 22 honeycomb|2<sub>22</sub>]]
|&nbsp;
|&nbsp;
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node_1|3|node|3|node}} = [[Birectified 2 22 honeycomb|0<sub>222</sub>]]
|-
| <math>{\tilde{E}}_7</math> = [3<sup>3,3,1</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodes_10r|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node}} = [[3 31 honeycomb|3<sub>31</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node_1}} = [[1 33 honeycomb|1<sub>33</sub>]]
|&nbsp;
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node_1|3|node}} = [[Rectified 1 33 honeycomb|0<sub>331</sub>]]
|-
| <math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> = [3<sup>5,2,1</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[2 51 honeycomb|2<sub>51</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_01lr|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[1 52 honeycomb|1<sub>52</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}} = [[5 21 honeycomb|5<sub>21</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_10|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[Rectified 1 52 honeycomb|0<sub>521</sub>]]
|}

There are three hyperbolic ([[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Ranks 4.E2.80.9310|paracompact]]) [[Coxeter group]]s in dimensions 7, 8, and 9:
{| class="wikitable"
!Coxeter group
!colspan=4|Honeycombs
|-
|<math>{\bar{T}}_7</math> = [3<sup>3,2,2</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node|3|node|3|node_1}} = [[3 22 honeycomb|3<sub>22</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodes_10r|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node|3|node|3|node}} = [[2 32 honeycomb|2<sub>32</sub>]]
|&nbsp;
|{{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node_1|3|node|3|node|3|node}} = [[Rectified 3 22 honeycomb|0<sub>322</sub>]]
|-
|<math>{\bar{T}}_8</math> = [3<sup>4,3,1</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[4 31 honeycomb|4<sub>31</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}} = [[3 41 honeycomb|3<sub>41</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_01lr|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[1 43 honeycomb|1<sub>43</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_10|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[Rectified 1 43 honeycomb|0<sub>431</sub>]]
|-
|<math>{\bar{T}}_9</math> = [3<sup>6,2,1</sup>]
|{{CDD|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[2 61 honeycomb|2<sub>61</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_01lr|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[1 62 honeycomb|1<sub>62</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}} = [[6 21 honeycomb|6<sub>21</sub>]]
|{{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_10|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = [[0 621 honeycomb|0<sub>621</sub>]]
|}

As a generalization more order-3 branches can also be expressed in this symbol. The 4-dimensional affine [[Coxeter group]], <math>{\tilde{Q}}_4</math>, [3<sup>1,1,1,1</sup>], has four order-3 branches, and can express one honeycomb, '''1<sub>111</sub>''', {{CDD|node_1|3|node|splitsplit1|branch3|node}}, represents a lower symmetry form of the [[16-cell honeycomb]], and '''0<sub>1111</sub>''', {{CDD|nodes|split2|node_1|split1|nodes}} for the [[rectified 16-cell honeycomb]]. The 5-dimensional hyperbolic [[Coxeter group]], <math>{\bar{L}}_4</math>, [3<sup>1,1,1,1,1</sup>], has five order-3 branches, and can express one honeycomb, '''1<sub>1111</sub>''', {{CDD|nodes|split2|node|splitsplit1|branch3|node_1}} and its rectification as '''0<sub>11111</sub>''', {{CDD|nodes|split2|node_1|splitsplit1|branch3|node}}.
